sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: What are we doing when we sketch an object to show it is 'on the move'?
options: A) Drawing stiff, straight lines
B) Capturing frozen shapes
C) Using action lines or tilted angles to show speed
D) Erasing the entire sketch
questions.answer: C) Using action lines or tilted angles to show speed

questions.question_text: Which technique helps create a 'Peeping Out of the Window' composition?
options: A) Drawing a border or frame around the outdoor scene
B) Drawing only the sky with no edges
C) Closing your eyes and painting
D) Drawing a microscopic view of a leaf
questions.answer: A) Drawing a border or frame around the outdoor scene

questions.question_text: What do we call a sequence of drawings inside boxes used for 'Picturing Stories'?
options: A) A sculpture
B) A storyboard or comic strip
C) A landscape painting
D) A still life arrangement
questions.answer: B) A storyboard or comic strip

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of creating an 'Imaginary Being'?
options: A) Drawing a normal house cat
B) Sketching a realistic apple
C) Combining a lion's body with an eagle's wings
D) Tracing a photograph of a car
questions.answer: C) Combining a lion's body with an eagle's wings

questions.question_text: When making a poster for 'Spreading the Message', what is the most important element?
options: A) Clear text and bold, eye-catching visuals
B) Very tiny, hidden letters
C) Using only gray and brown colors
D) Leaving the paper mostly blank
questions.answer: A) Clear text and bold, eye-catching visuals

questions.question_text: When you 'Create a Scene', how do you show that an object is far away in the background?
options: A) Draw it very large and dark
B) Draw it upside down
C) Draw it smaller and higher up on the paper
D) Draw it with very thick outlines
questions.answer: C) Draw it smaller and higher up on the paper

questions.question_text: Which materials are primarily used for 'Stitch it for a Story' activities?
options: A) Wet clay and a pottery wheel
B) A needle, colorful threads, and fabric
C) Watercolors and a thick brush
D) Scissors and cardboard only
questions.answer: B) A needle, colorful threads, and fabric

questions.question_text: What does the 'Time Team Technique' usually refer to in an art class?
options: A) Working alone in complete silence
B) Tearing up your artwork
C) Collaborating on a group project like a large mural
D) Finishing a painting in one minute
questions.answer: C) Collaborating on a group project like a large mural

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of the 'View and Review' process in art?
options: A) To observe artworks and share constructive feedback
B) To hide your artwork from everyone else
C) To paint over someone else's drawing
D) To throw away old sketches
questions.answer: A) To observe artworks and share constructive feedback

questions.question_text: If you want to draw a ball bouncing down some stairs, what is the best way to show its path?
options: A) A single, perfectly straight line
B) A dotted, curved line following the bounces
C) A thick black square
D) A highly detailed shadow underneath it
questions.answer: B) A dotted, curved line following the bounces

questions.question_text: Describe how you would use framing to draw a scene looking out of your bedroom window. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: I would draw the window frame along the edges of my paper, then sketch the trees, roads, and houses outside to make the viewer feel like they are looking through it.

questions.question_text: Why are facial expressions important when picturing a story in a comic strip? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Facial expressions help show the characters' feelings, such as joy or sadness, allowing the reader to understand the mood and plot of the story without needing too many words.

questions.question_text: Name two key features of an effective poster designed for 'Spreading the Message' about saving trees. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: An effective poster should have a short, catchy slogan in bold letters and a bright, powerful drawing that immediately catches the viewer's attention and clearly shows the environmental message.

questions.question_text: How can embroidery or stitching be used to tell a visual story on a piece of fabric? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Stitching can be used to sew outlines of characters, animals, and trees using different colored threads. We can create scenes sequentially on pieces of cloth to narrate a traditional tale.

questions.question_text: Why is it important to review and appreciate your classmates' artwork during the 'View and Review' session? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Reviewing helps us learn new techniques from our peers. It allows us to give positive feedback, encouraging creativity while helping everyone improve their artistic skills together.

questions.question_text: Imagine you have created an 'Imaginary Being' that lives in the clouds. Describe its physical appearance and the colors you would use to paint it. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: My imaginary being has the soft body of a sheep made entirely of glowing pink clouds and the wide, golden wings of an eagle. It has large, sparkling blue eyes. I would use pastel pinks, bright gold, and sky blue to make it look magical and light.

questions.question_text: Imagine creating a busy marketplace scene. Describe the elements you would place in the foreground, middle ground, and background to create depth. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: In the foreground, I would draw large, detailed fruit baskets and vendors. In the middle ground, I would sketch people walking and buying things, drawing them slightly smaller. In the background, I would paint small, faded shops and distant hills to give the scene a realistic sense of depth.

questions.question_text: Explain the step-by-step action plan you and your friends would follow to create a collaborative mural on a school wall using the 'Team Technique'. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, we would hold a team meeting to sketch our ideas on paper and agree on a final theme. Next, we would divide tasks, assigning some friends to draw the outlines on the wall and others to mix the paints. Finally, we would work together side-by-side to paint the mural, blending our colors harmoniously.

questions.question_text: Explain how you would draw a racing car to express intense speed and motion on a flat piece of paper. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: I would draw the racing car with an angled, aerodynamic posture, leaning slightly forward. Behind the tires, I would add thick, horizontal action lines and clouds of swirling dust to express rapid forward motion. The background features would be slightly blurred to create the illusion that the car is speeding past them quickly.
